newsitem.title: USA: Thirsty US refiners lure foreign sweet crudes.
newsitem.headline: Thirsty US refiners lure foreign sweet crudes.

text.p: Thirsty U.S. refiners were seen luring foreign sweet crudes into the Gulf Coast on Wednesday, as prices steadily creeped up.
Several foreign crude sellers, keeping an eye on the rising premium for domestic Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James, have begun to show Brent crude into the Gulf Coast.
LLS, the closest domestic competitor to Brent, fetched 23-26 cents over West Texas Intermediate/Cushing on Wednesday, up from plus 22-24 cents on Tuesday.
A U.S. company and a U.S. trading house were each showing Brent for end-August delivery into the Gulf at around 30-35 cents under WTI/Cushing, traders said.
A Norwegian company was still showing a 15-20 August Brent at around the same level.
Talk was circulating about a possible September 5-10 delivery as well, traders said.
Brent was last sold into the Gulf at around 35 cents under WTI, traders said.
Among other North Sea crudes, at least two cargoes of Norwegian Oseberg were sold to different buyers on Wednesday at an unspecified discount to WTI, traders said.
Elsewhere, equity producer British Petroleum sold a cargo of Colombian Cusiana crude oil at 85 cents a barrel under benchmark West Texas Intermediate/Cushing fob, trade sources said.
The gasoline-rich grade was last placed at 90 cents under WTI.
The discount has decreased over the past week in response to the narrow WTI/Brent spread and softening freight rates in the Caribbean, trade sources said.
Five more August cargoes of Cusiana, plus a cross-month loader into September, were still available.
